cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Obey Without Explanation
cards.instruction: Create increasingly inconvenient requests that test whether someone accepts your authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Bring that empty box to my desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What do you need it for?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. At present, to establish whether you'll bring it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Take it back without the question this time.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 orders the box and A3 defers questions expressly to test obedience; A5 requires a return without questioning, so assumed rank shapes the test.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 asks purpose, A3 makes compliance the purpose; B4 confirms completion, which A5 uses to order the reverse journey.

relationship.evidence: B2 reasonably wants to know why and B4 complies; B does not need to resist every request for the test to become visible.

heightening.evidence: B4 successful delivery causes A5 additional inconvenience plus removal of B question privilege.

specificity.evidence: A1 empty box and desk define a simple task; A3 states why the pointless errand matters to A.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 take it back earns the circular errand from B4 arrival; A3 stock prefix is wordy but functionally denies questioning.
